findings.title: Reschedule cancellation does not await calendar/video deletions
findings.body: Using `forEach(async ...)` discards every callback promise. Before this change, `getCalendar()` was synchronous, so `deleteEvent()` was invoked before the callback returned; now the callback suspends on the dynamic import and the mutation proceeds to send email/webhooks and return without waiting for (or handling errors from) any external deletion. The booking is already marked CANCELLED, so a request-reschedule can leave the old calendar/video meeting active and any import/deletion failure becomes an unhandled rejection. Build an array of deletion promises and `await Promise.all` (with explicit error handling).

findings.title: Vital reschedules fire-and-forget external resource deletion
findings.body: The async callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited by the surrounding `try/catch`. Since `getCalendar` now awaits a dynamic import, this function can finish and send the reschedule email before it has even called `deleteEvent`; failures after the await also bypass the catch block. The booking has already been cancelled at this point, so external Vital calendar/video events can remain active. Collect the callback promises and await them, preferably with per-integration error handling.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation omits dynamically imported calendar deletions from awaited work
findings.body: The recurring-event path starts an `async forEach` over calendar credentials, but does not await its callbacks. Each callback now waits for `getCalendar` before pushing deletion promises into `apiDeletes`; the handler subsequently reaches `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` while `apiDeletes` is still empty or incomplete. As a result, the cancellation response and database cleanup can complete before recurring external events are deleted, and import/delete failures are unhandled. Replace the `forEach` with awaited promise collection (or an awaited loop) and add the resulting deletion promises before the final `Promise.all`.
